triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov
triples.quote: He had a brace of fine dueling pistols in a case, which he had not pawned till then because he prized them above all his possessions.

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: She had detested him from the first because he was engaged to Katerina Ivanovna

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: You have most likely heard of my cousin, Madame Belmesov. Her husband was ruined, ‘had come to grief,’ as you characteristically express it, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: I’m quarreling with my steward about it, and I’ve just borrowed five hundred roubles from Miüsov, myself. No, no, I’ve no money.

triples.subject: Shtchedrin
triples.quote: He has taught me so much, so much about the vocation of woman. So last year I sent him an anonymous letter of two lines: ‘I kiss and embrace you, my teacher, for the modern woman. Persevere.’

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov
triples.quote: And she actually put the cord round his neck, and began arranging it. In extreme embarrassment, Mitya bent down and helped her, and at last he got it under his neck-tie and collar through his shirt to his chest.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov
triples.quote: “Oh, the devil!” roared Mitya, and with all his might brought his fist down on the table. “Aie! Aie!” cried Madame Hohlakov, alarmed, and she flew to the other end of the drawing-room.
